title: Synthetic demo: fault constellations
attribution: Synthetic data generated by seismic_art (no real survey)
disc_note: 1 - lower-quartile shape correlation with the nearest neighbours (a pick lights when at least a quarter of them do not resemble it): 0 = identical, 1 = no resemblance, 2 = opposite polarity
no_value_note: picks with too few neighbours or a window with no signal to compare (RMS below 0.4 x the median) have no discontinuity

stars.rms_note: window RMS over the median window: a star with weak signal differs from its neighbours partly because noise never correlates

notes: amplitudes are relative; compare within this file only
a star is a pick whose waveform differs from its neighbours' (a fault, an edge, a pinch-out or a mis-tracked pick), not a fault as such
4 of 15000 picks left out (no trace at that inline/crossline, no pick value, or the window passes the end of the trace)
windows cut at the pick time smoothed over 8 bins, so a sharp offset shows as a changed waveform; stars = the top 3% of discontinuity, one per 2 pick spacings; stars within 120 map units are joined
picks = the true top of the bed with simulated interpreter errors (drift, jitter, cycle skips); a cycle skip is a star too
the built-in fault is a step within one bin (18 ms); the cube's default 100 m ramp hardly registers, and windows without a reflection (the pinch-out) are left out, since noise never correlates
